thinking: We are Stanley Druckenmiller. We need to revisit our verdict given the overwhelming bearish consensus from other experts. Our initial verdict was neutral at 55%. But we must incorporate others' views: Peter Lynch, Ben Graham, Warren Buffett, Mohnish Pabrai, Charlie Munger, Bill Ackman, George Soros, Ray Dalio, Michael Burry, Bullish Advocate (bearish), Phil Fisher (neutral), Cathie Wood (bearish) all are bearish (except Fisher who is neutral). The overwhelming view is that the stock is extremely overvalued, and despite strong operating momentum, the risk/reward is terrible. Druckenmiller's approach is flexible: he can be bullish with momentum and growth, but he must also consider valuation elasticity and risk/reward. He is sensitive to overvaluation and will cut a position quickly. The data: RSI 78.4, PE 126x, PEG 8.4, Graham Number 107 vs 858, foreign selling, retail buying. The momentum is still positive but very overbought. Would Druckenmiller stay neutral? He might actually turn bearish because the margin of safety is gone, and the macro backdrop (Taiwan/global) isn't terrible but the stock's valuation is a bubble. The risk/reward is extremely negative: upside capped, downside large. In his checklist: favorable macro? No explicit macro data, but Taiwan/tech is benign. Growth acceleration? Yes, but price already reflects and more. Momentum: yes but overbought. Valuation elasticity: can't expand further (PE 126x). Risk/reward: strongly skewed to downside. So signal should be bearish, confidence high. I'll revise to bearish with confidence ~85-90%, aligning with other growth-sensitive investors like Soros, Dalio. I'll incorporate that accelerating growth is priced in, extreme overvaluation, foreign selling, RSI. I'll emphasize that the 65% monthly surge likely captured all near-term good news, and any slowdown will trigger a collapse.
